about.lede: We make plain things and sell them plainly. The label says what is inside, the price says what it costs, and a person answers the email.
about.numbers.logos: logos on the front of anything we sell

about.story.2: We have added a few more since, and a plan or two for people who come back. The labels are still plain. The prices are still on the front.
about.story.label: the story so far
about.story.title: one product, one plain label

about.team.title: the people behind the shelf

features.art.keep: KEEP IN A COOL DRY DATABASE
features.art.label: White generic packs with blue stripes on a shelf: a box labelled website, a can labelled blog, a carton labelled pages and a bag labelled copy.
features.bento.access.caption: contrast for running text, in every look
features.bento.access.text: WCAG 2.2 AA throughout, and AAA where a site can hold it: every page is checked in all four looks, at three widths.
features.bento.access.title: open to every reader
features.bento.once.text: A price, a portrait, a name: each lives in one row, and every place that shows it reads that row. Change a plan's price in Notion and the pricing page, the homepage, the comparison table and what search engines and assistants read all follow, with nothing to hunt down.
features.bento.once.title: change it once
features.bento.privacy.caption: third-party requests from a reader's browser
features.bento.privacy.text: A reader's browser talks to your site and nobody else.
features.bento.privacy.title: private by construction
features.bento.publishing.text: Date a post for next Tuesday at 4pm, tick Published, and it waits for the minute.
features.bento.publishing.title: scheduled, not rushed
features.bento.title: and it behaves
features.copy.fallbacks.body: If Notion cannot be reached, the site keeps its last good answer, then the copy captured at build time. It never fills a gap with words that are not in your Notion.
features.copy.fallbacks.title: Notion down, site up
features.copy.formatting.body: Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and code in a slot or in a row's words are drawn as Notion shows them. Notion's colours stay in a page's body, so the web copy keeps the site's look.
features.copy.formatting.title: Formatting comes through
features.copy.intro: Every piece of text on a designed page is a slot. Each slot looks for a row in the Notion database with its name.
features.copy.keys.body: npm run copy renders the site and lists every slot with suggested words. npm run notion:check names any slot with no row, and npm run notion:seed-copy adds them, unticked, for you to read and tick (it needs an integration with Insert content).
features.copy.keys.title: Every slot listed
features.copy.links.body: A link made in Notion stays a link on the site. Only web, mail, phone and on-site links are drawn; anything else is drawn as its words. A link to another site opens in a new tab.
features.copy.links.title: Links survive
features.copy.once.body: A fact lives in one row, and every place that shows it reads that row: a plan's price feeds the pricing page, the homepage, the comparison table, llms.txt and the search data; a person's portrait every byline and the team page; the site's name every title and share card. Change it once.
features.copy.once.title: Written once, shown everywhere
features.copy.states.body: A ticked row shows Notion's words. An unticked row, a ticked one left empty, or no row at all shows nothing, so no word reaches the site unseen. Only the starter site, before Notion is connected, shows the words in the code, and a control's own name (a field's label, a button) falls back to them rather than go blank.
features.copy.states.title: Three states per slot
features.copy.title: Words, from Notion
features.cta.note: Free. Open source. MIT licence. Runs on Notion.
features.demo.label: serving suggestion
features.demo.lead: Every slot on the site reads a row in Notion. A ticked row: its words. An unticked row, a ticked one left empty, or no row at all: nothing, so no word reaches the site unseen. Only the starter site, before Notion is connected, shows the words written into the code.
features.demo.none.rule: Shows nothing: a word must be in Notion to show
features.demo.region: The three states, side by side
features.demo.title: one sentence, three states
features.deploy.button.text: Either way ends the same: your own copy of the code in your GitHub, a project on Vercel that builds from it, and these two settings in that project: the token from step 2, and the link to your copy of the template (Share → Copy link; the whole link works).
features.deploy.button.title: Put the code on Vercel, one of two ways
features.deploy.connect.text: In Notion's integrations, make an internal one with Read content and nothing else, and copy its token. Then, on your copy of the template, open ⋯ → Connections and add it.
features.deploy.connect.title: Make an integration
features.deploy.domain.text: Add your domain in Vercel and set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL to it. Then connect an email platform, or the contact form and the mailing list stay examples that send nothing. For rate limits shared across every server, add Upstash (Redis) from Storage → Marketplace and redeploy. A Shopify or Printify shop is a setting or two, when you want one.
features.deploy.domain.title: Point your domain, connect your email
features.deploy.github.text: On the template's GitHub page, press Use this template, then Create a new repository (or Fork it). In Vercel, press Add New → Project, pick your copy and press Import. Add the two settings under Environment Variables, then press Deploy.
features.deploy.github.title: From GitHub
features.deploy.label: directions
features.deploy.notion.text: Open the template in Notion and press Duplicate. Your copy has every page, post, plan, product and word of this site, ready to rename.
features.deploy.notion.title: Duplicate the Notion template
features.deploy.oneclick.text: Press Deploy on Vercel and sign in with GitHub. Vercel makes the copy in your GitHub and the project in one go, then asks for the two settings. Press Deploy.
features.deploy.oneclick.title: In one press
features.deploy.posthog.open: Every PostHog step, the feedback agent included
features.deploy.posthog.text: For analytics and the Feedback button. In PostHog, copy the project token (Settings → Project) and set it in Vercel, with the region if your project is in the US cloud. Then make a personal API key (Settings → User → Personal API keys: read on Project and Organization, write on Survey and Feature flag) and set it too. Redeploy: the build makes the Site feedback survey and the flags, and nothing is counted until a reader says yes.
features.deploy.posthog.title: Switch on PostHog
features.deploy.steps: About ten minutes, most of it waiting for the first deploy, and nothing to install. A Notion account, a GitHub account and a Vercel account, all free, put it live. The contact form and the mailing list also need an email platform, such as Brevo or Resend.
features.deploy.title: deploy on vercel in five steps
features.deploy.write.text: Tick Published. The site follows within a minute, or within seconds with a webhook.
features.deploy.write.title: Write in Notion
features.facts.cost: Cost to run on free plans
features.facts.google: Fonts fetched from Google by readers
features.facts.heading: nothing artificial
features.facts.label: on the side of the tin
features.facts.lede: The numbers below are true of the code as it ships, not of a good day.
features.facts.note: Pages are built ahead. Notion is asked for the words once a minute at most, whatever the traffic, and about a picture only when no cache holds it yet. Cost counted on the free plans of Notion, the email platforms and Vercel (whose free plan is for personal sites).
features.facts.publish: Time from Notion to the site
features.facts.title: Nutrition facts
features.help: Would rather somebody else set it up, or make it look like yours?
features.jump.label: On this page
features.kinds.caption: The Kind of a row says what it makes. Nothing appears until Published is ticked and its Published Date, to the minute, has come; Status is for your team.
features.kinds.copy: One piece of the site’s wording, such as a heading or a button: Title says which (home.hero.title), Text is what it says. A few hold a picture in Image instead, the site’s own logo (site.logo) and icon (site.icon) among them.
features.kinds.logo: A tool the site works with, in the “goes well with” strip, its mark in Image. The site’s own logo is not one: it is the site.logo row.
features.kinds.menu: A link in the header or the footer: Title names the page, Slug the menu, Order its place. Unticked, it is off the menu.
features.kinds.page: A page at /its-slug, written in the row’s own page body. Layout Landing makes it a landing page of sections.
features.kinds.person: Somebody on /team, and the author of the posts that name them: Title is the name, Description the role, Text a line about them, Image the portrait. Team Page Off makes a guest: on their posts, off /team.
features.kinds.plan: A plan on /pricing: its price (empty is custom pricing), a yearly price, its features one a line, and its button.
features.kinds.post: A blog post at /blog/its-slug, with its date, author, category and tags. Category Releases makes it a release: on /changelog instead of the blog.
features.kinds.product: A product at /shop/its-slug: price, pictures, a description, stock, and how it is bought.
features.kinds.question: A question on /questions, its answer in Text. Category Pricing puts it on /pricing too; Template, on this page.
features.kinds.quote: A quotation: Text is what was said, Title is who said it. The homepage shows the first, /pricing the next.
features.kinds.redirect: A short link: /go/its-title sends people to its Link.
features.kinds.resource: A line on /resources: a title, a description and a link.
features.kinds.review: A review on the homepage: Title is the name, Text what they said, Rating the stars, Published Date when, Image their photo (none: their initials). Tag Example marks an invented one.
features.kinds.section: Where a section of a page goes: Title names it, Slug the page, Order its place. Unticked, it is off; two rows, it shows twice.
features.kinds.title: Contents
features.label: a notion-powered cms
features.lede: This site is a live demo of the template, and Notion is its CMS. Copy, pages, posts, plans and products live in one database: tick Published and the site follows. The full list of ingredients is one press away. Nothing hidden, nothing artificial.
features.list.lede: Ten groups, every one written out, with what is not included. It is a long list, so it has a page of its own.
features.list.page.lede: Everything the template does, group by group, and what it leaves out. Nothing hidden, nothing artificial.
features.list.title: the full list of ingredients
features.logos.label: Works with
features.mail.example.body: Until a platform is set up, both forms are marked as examples, send nothing anywhere, and say so when pressed.
features.mail.example.title: Examples until connected
features.mail.intro: A contact form and a mailing list, sent through an email platform of yours. The site needs one to send anything: it keeps no addresses and sends no email itself.
features.mail.platforms.body: Brevo (which also makes its own list), Resend and SendGrid run both forms. Mailchimp, Klaviyo, beehiiv, Loops, MailerLite, Kit and Buttondown keep the list, and Postmark sends the messages: pair one of each. Double opt-in is the platform's to ask.
features.mail.platforms.title: Built in
features.mail.spam.body: Rate limits, a honeypot field, and a server that checks every field again. Nothing personal is written to the logs.
features.mail.spam.title: Quietly guarded
features.mail.title: Email, on your own platform
features.mail.webhook.body: A webhook, signed when you set a secret, sends each sign-up and message to Zapier, Make, n8n or your own endpoint.
features.mail.webhook.title: Anything else
features.media.alt.body: A caption line that starts Alt: is a picture's description, read to screen readers and never shown, and a product's picture is described by its name. npm run notion:check names any picture nobody described.
features.media.alt.title: Pictures described in Notion
features.media.covers.body: A post's or a page's cover is printed in the look's own colour, so a photograph from anywhere sits with the site. Set Cover Tint to Off and it shows as uploaded (in mono it stays grey).
features.media.covers.title: Covers in the site's colours
features.media.hero.body: Give the home page's hero a photograph from Notion and it fills the width of the window under a veil, with the words light on it, in every look.
features.media.hero.title: A picture under the hero
features.media.intro: Notion's file links expire after an hour and live on somebody else's host. Here every picture and file is served from your site.
features.media.proxy.body: Each picture and file gets a signed /media/ address. The server fetches it from Notion only when no cache holds it yet, and caches it for a year.
features.media.proxy.title: Signed addresses
features.media.sized.body: Upload a large photograph and each reader is sent it near the size their screen shows it, as WebP, so a portrait an inch wide is not a download of megabytes. A drawing, a GIF and a file over 40 MB go as they are.
features.media.sized.title: The size it is shown
features.media.title: Pictures and files, from your own domain
features.media.video.body: YouTube and Vimeo appear as a card. Nothing loads from them until the reader presses play.
features.media.video.title: Videos load when asked
features.not.accounts: Accounts, logins and comments. It is a website, not an app.
features.not.lockin: Lock-in. Your words are in your Notion; the code is yours under MIT.
features.not.title: Not included
features.not.uploads: Uploads from readers. Nothing on the site accepts a file.
features.pages.addresses.body: A page lives at its Slug, nested if you like (guides/setup). A page that would take a built-in page's address, or one another page holds, is skipped, and npm run notion:check says which.
features.pages.addresses.title: Your addresses
features.pages.blocks.body: Paragraphs, four sizes of heading, toggle headings, bulleted, numbered and to-do lists, toggles, quotes, callouts, dividers, code, equations, tables, columns, tables of contents, images, video, audio, PDFs, files, bookmarks, embeds, link previews, synced blocks and links to other pages.
features.pages.blocks.title: The blocks you write with
features.pages.blog.body: Dates, categories and tags with pages of their own, featured posts, reading time, newer and older links, a search box and an RSS feed. Authors are Person rows, written once: one portrait and job title on every byline and on the team page, and a guest is a Person row kept off it.
features.pages.blog.title: A proper blog
features.pages.brand.body: Upload a logo in Notion and it stands where the mark does, in the header and the footer, with a version for the dark look if you like. Your icon, or the logo, becomes the browser tab's and the home screen's, made at every size each needs.
features.pages.brand.title: Your logo and icon
features.pages.intro: Add a row, set its Kind to Page or Post, write the page body in Notion, tick Published.
features.pages.looks.body: Light, dark, mono and rainbow, or whatever the reader's system prefers. Every pairing of colours is checked for contrast in each, to WCAG AAA, and the choice stays in the reader's browser.
features.pages.looks.title: Four looks
features.pages.menus.body: A Menu row turns a link in the header or the footer off, moves it, or adds a page of your own. The header holds at most four links left of the mark and two right of it, so it stays level.
features.pages.menus.title: Menus you arrange
features.pages.more.body: /questions from Question rows (Category Pricing puts one on /pricing too), /team and /about from Person rows, /resources from Resource rows, and /changelog from posts filed under Releases, which stay out of the blog.
features.pages.more.title: Pages made of rows
features.pages.schedule.body: Give a post, or any row, a Published Date in the future, with a time and its time zone if you like (4pm GMT on the 1st), and tick Published: it appears then, without anybody pressing anything. A date with no time starts at midnight UTC.
features.pages.schedule.title: Scheduled posts
features.pages.sections.body: On the homepage, /pricing, /about, /team, /security and /questions, a Section row turns a section off, moves it to another of them, puts a page in a new order or shows a section twice. The hero stays first, and a section with no row stays where it was designed.
features.pages.sections.title: Pages you can rearrange
features.pages.style.body: Cover and icon as Notion sets them, the Default, Serif and Mono fonts and full width from the row's Font and Full width (Notion's own page menu is not in its API), and Notion's nine text and background colours, in every look.
features.pages.style.title: Notion's page options
features.pages.title: Pages and posts, written in Notion
features.pricing.compare.body: Built from the plans' own feature lines: a real table, with headers a screen reader can follow.
features.pricing.compare.title: A comparison table
features.pricing.intro: The parts of a SaaS site, as rows and blocks in Notion.
features.pricing.landing.body: Set a page's Layout to Landing and its blocks become sections: columns become cards, a run of short figures in callouts a row of numbers, toggles questions, a quote a quotation, and a line of links buttons.
features.pricing.landing.title: Landing pages
features.pricing.plans.body: Monthly and yearly prices, a recommended plan, features as lines, and the saving worked out rather than typed.
features.pricing.plans.title: Plans
features.pricing.proof.body: Quote rows fill the quotations, and Proof Logos rows the strip of tools the site goes well with, which names the tools it is built on until you add your own. Reviews tagged Example show as examples, and only until a real one is published.
features.pricing.proof.title: Quotes, logos and reviews
features.pricing.title: Pricing and landing pages
features.privacy.analytics.body: PostHog and Google Analytics are off until you add a key, and then count nothing until the reader says yes. Both go through your server, which shortens IP addresses.
features.privacy.analytics.title: Analytics only after a yes
features.privacy.cookies.body: A bag of cookies, a plain box or a banner along the bottom, chosen in Notion. Every shape asks the same question, no is as easy as yes, and Escape answers no.
features.privacy.cookies.title: The cookie question, your shape
features.privacy.fonts.body: The faces are files in the repository, served from your domain; nothing is fetched from Google, at build time or by a reader. A Content-Security-Policy refuses any font or stylesheet from elsewhere.
features.privacy.fonts.title: Fonts from your own files
features.privacy.intro: A reader's browser talks to your site and nobody else, until they press play on a video or go to the checkout.
features.privacy.limits.body: Every route a reader can call is rate limited; with Upstash or Vercel KV, one count holds across every server, kept as a hash, never an address. /.well-known/security.txt names your own contact and renews itself daily.
features.privacy.limits.title: Rate limits, and a security.txt
features.privacy.secrets.body: Every key and address is an environment variable, listed in .env.example. A test fails if anything that looks like a secret is committed, or if the list and the code disagree.
features.privacy.secrets.title: No secrets in the code
features.privacy.title: Privacy, by construction
features.publishing.intro: Edit in Notion. The site follows.
features.publishing.minute.body: Content is read from Notion once a minute at most, however busy the site is, and pages refresh in the background.
features.publishing.minute.title: Within about a minute
features.publishing.redirects.body: A Redirect row makes /go/its-title send people wherever its Link says. Print the short link on a poster, or as a QR code (npm run qr), and change the destination later.
features.publishing.redirects.title: Short links for print
features.publishing.status.body: Draft, In Review and Published say where a row is, kept in step with the Published box by two automations. The site reads Published alone, and the Scheduled view lists what waits for its date.
features.publishing.status.title: Status for your team
features.publishing.title: Publishing
features.publishing.webhooks.body: Point a Notion webhook or a database automation at the site, with a secret of its own, and it refreshes the moment something changes.
features.publishing.webhooks.title: Or within seconds
features.quality.access.body: 7:1 contrast in all four looks, 44-pixel targets, a 3-pixel focus ring, nothing moving for readers who ask for stillness, and a select and tabs that keep the whole keyboard.
features.quality.access.title: Accessible, to AAA where a site can be
features.quality.audits.body: An accessibility audit (axe at WCAG 2.2 AAA, with contrast, target sizes and the focus ring measured in every look at three widths), a privacy audit that fails on any request leaving the site, and a sharpness audit for pictures a retina screen would stretch.
features.quality.audits.title: Audits
features.quality.feedback.body: A Feedback button sends a reader's words to your PostHog survey through your site, needing no yes and passing on no address. Turn on the agent and it reads them and opens draft pull requests for a person to review.
features.quality.feedback.title: Feedback from readers
features.quality.intro: Rules a reader would notice breaking are tests.
features.quality.tests.body: Every page is rendered three ways (with no Notion, from a stand-in Notion over HTTP, and with an empty database) and checked for alt text, named controls, working links and structured data.
features.quality.tests.title: Over a thousand tests
features.quality.title: Tested
features.questions.title: questions about the template
features.rows.1.text: The editor you already use. Headings, toggles, tables, pictures: the blocks you write with come out as you wrote them.
features.rows.1.title: write in notion
features.rows.2.text: Nothing goes out until you say so. Date a post next week and it waits for the day.
features.rows.2.title: tick published
features.rows.3.text: Within a minute, or within seconds with a webhook. No build to run, no editor to log in to.
features.rows.3.title: the site follows
features.rows.lede: The words on the pages, the pages themselves, the posts, the plans and the products. One Notion database, a Kind on each row.
features.rows.title: every word is a row
features.search.data.body: Pages, posts, the blog, the questions, the team, the site with its logo and the maker, and a live shop's products, described in schema.org JSON-LD, with breadcrumbs, real dates and nothing invented. No review is marked up.
features.search.data.title: Structured data
features.search.intro: The same words feed every machine that reads the site.
features.search.maps.body: A sitemap, an RSS feed, llms.txt and llms-full.txt with the plans and their prices, and every page, post and product written in Notion as Markdown at its address with .md added, for the assistants people ask. Once it is set up, IndexNow tells Bing and the engines that share it after each deploy, and each hour what changed in Notion.
features.search.maps.title: Sitemap, RSS, llms.txt, Markdown
features.search.meta.body: Every page gets a title, a description, a canonical address and a share card: a picture you give it in Notion, its cover, or one drawn in the house style with its own title on it.
features.search.meta.title: Titles, descriptions, share cards
features.search.starter.body: Until Notion is connected, every page is noindex and robots are shut, so the starter content never competes in search.
features.search.starter.title: Out of search until it is yours
features.search.title: Search and sharing
features.shelf.blog.text: Posts with dates, categories, tags and a feed. Tick Published and it is out.
features.shelf.blog.title: blog
features.shelf.copy.text: Every word on the site is a row. Change it in Notion and the site follows.
features.shelf.copy.title: copy
features.shelf.pages.text: Write a page in Notion and it is a page here, drawn as Notion draws it.
features.shelf.pages.title: pages
features.shelf.website.text: The whole site in one box: pages, a blog, a shop and plans, live in five steps.
features.shelf.website.title: website
features.shop.cart.body: Kept in the reader's own browser, written only when they add something, and every change announced to screen readers as it happens.
features.shop.cart.title: A cart that stays put
features.shop.catalogue.body: Names, descriptions, prices, stock and pictures, and from Shopify the sizes, are kept in Shopify or Printify and copied in, never typed twice. Change a product there, run npm run shop:import -- --write, and the site follows.
features.shop.catalogue.title: One catalogue, kept in your shop
features.shop.example.body: Until a way to sell is set up, the shop says it is an example, switches the checkout off and keeps itself out of search.
features.shop.example.title: An example until it is real
features.shop.intro: Your products stay where you sell them. One command copies them in as rows, and the shelves, the product pages and the cart follow.
features.shop.notion.body: Which products show, which come first, what address each has, Low stock and Pre-order, and any picture you upload in Notion. Anything else the shop says that was changed in Notion is changed back, so the two cannot drift.
features.shop.notion.title: What Notion decides
features.shop.printify.body: Each product's button goes to its page in your Printify store, which takes the order and makes it.
features.shop.printify.title: Or a Printify Pop-Up Store
features.shop.shopify.body: The cart checks out at your Shopify shop, which prices the order from its own records. Printify connected to that shop fulfils it.
features.shop.shopify.title: Checkout with Shopify

privacy.analytics.body: Only after you say yes in the cookie notice, we record which pages are opened and what is done on them: what is pressed, what goes in a cart, when a form is sent, and errors a page runs into. It all goes through this site, which shortens your IP address before passing anything on, and takes names and addresses out of page addresses.
privacy.analytics.google: Google Analytics counts them as well, and Google may handle what it receives in the United States ([Google's privacy policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy)).
privacy.analytics.none: This site counts nothing. There are no analytics and no tracking cookies.
privacy.analytics.posthog.eu: PostHog counts the visits for us, on its servers in the European Union ([its privacy policy](https://posthog.com/privacy)).
privacy.analytics.posthog.us: PostHog counts the visits for us, on its servers in the United States ([its privacy policy](https://posthog.com/privacy)).
privacy.cookies.title: Cookies and storage
privacy.forms.chat: If this site has a support chat, it is PostHog's, and it appears only after you say yes to cookies. It sends what you write, and the email and name you give it, to PostHog, which we use to answer you, with the visit it came from. Your browser keeps the conversation so you can pick it up again, and a no to cookies deletes it.
privacy.forms.contact: The contact form sends us your name, address and message, with your company and what it is about if you gave them. The site does not store it; our mailbox does, for as long as the conversation needs.
privacy.forms.feedback: The Feedback button sends what you write, with the page you were on, the browser you use (its name and version), the look you had and the size of your window, to PostHog, which we use to read it. If you said yes to cookies, it also sends which visit it came from, so we can see what went wrong. It never sends your address or your name.
privacy.forms.list: The mailing list keeps your address and, if you give one, your first name, so we can send you the emails you asked for. Every email has an unsubscribe link, and unsubscribing is the end of it.
privacy.forms.processors: Both are handled for us by
privacy.forms.title: If you write to us or join the list
privacy.lede: What this website keeps about you. Not much.
privacy.rights.body: You can ask what we hold about you, have it corrected or deleted, object to how it is used, or take it elsewhere. Ask through the contact page and we will answer within a month. If you are unhappy with the answer, you can complain to your data protection authority.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.short.body: Your browser talks to this site and nobody else. Nothing is counted unless you say yes. If you write to us or join the mailing list, we keep what you sent, and only to answer you or send you the emails you asked for.
privacy.short.title: The short version.
privacy.table.cart: What you put in the cart, written only once you add something. Stays in your browser until you empty it.
privacy.table.chat: PostHog's support chat, if this site has one: the conversation you started, and the email and name you gave it, so you can carry on. Only after a yes, and a later no deletes it.
privacy.table.consent: Remembers your answer to the cookie notice. Stays in your browser.
privacy.table.google: Google Analytics: a random identifier, so a visit is counted once. Only after a yes.
privacy.table.name: Name
privacy.table.posthog: PostHog: a random identifier, kept as this cookie and in the storage of your browser, so a visit is counted once. Only after a yes, and a later no deletes both.
privacy.table.region: What this site keeps in your browser
privacy.table.theme: Remembers the look you chose (light, dark, mono or rainbow), if you chose one. Stays in your browser.
privacy.third.body: Fonts, pictures and files are served from this site, never fetched by your browser from anybody else. A YouTube or Vimeo video loads only if you press play, and from then on that video is between you and them.
privacy.third.hosting: Like any website, the company hosting this one keeps short-lived server logs, including IP addresses, to keep the site running and secure.
privacy.third.limits: To stop any one visitor flooding the site, Upstash counts the requests each one makes, a minute at a time. It never learns who: it is given a stand-in for your IP address, scrambled with a key it does not have, and each count is gone within the minute.
